plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pink. It thrives in cool, shaded woodland conditions and is prized for flowering in the depths of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to late winter (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: A glossy-leaved evergreen shrub or small tree bearing large, showy, rose-like flowers with bright yellow stamens. It prefers acidic, well-drained soil and partial shade, and thousands of cultivars exist.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and eastern China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, the UK, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil.

plants.name: Delosperma cooperi
plants.description: A mat-forming succulent perennial with fleshy leaves and daisy-like, vivid magenta flowers that open in bright sun. In the Southern Hemisphere summer it flowers heavily in sunny, well-drained sites.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February there); late spring to autumn in cooler northern regions
plants.location: Native to the Eastern Cape and Free State of South Africa; grown in rock gardens and as groundcover worldwide
plants.funFact: The flowers close in cloudy weather and at night, and the glistening, bladder-like cells on the leaves give the ice plant its name.

plants.name: Metrosideros excelsa
plants.description: A rugged evergreen coastal tree that is covered in brilliant crimson, brush-like flowers made up of masses of long stamens. It clings to cliffs and rocky shores and can form huge, sprawling, multi-trunked crowns.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (late November to January)
plants.location: Native to the coasts of New Zealand's North Island; planted in parts of Australia, South Africa, California and Chile
plants.funFact: Its flowering around Christmas has made it a New Zealand symbol of the festive season, and it is revered in Māori tradition.
